'''Colin John Bushnell''' (1947 – 1 January 2021) was a British mathematician specialising in [[number theory]] and [[representation theory]]. He spent most of his career at [[King's College London]], including a stint as the head of the School of Physical Sciences and Engineering, and made several contributions to the representation theory of [[reductive group|reductive]] [[p-adic group|''p''-adic group]]s and the [[local Langlands correspondence]].

==Early life and education==
Bushnell was born in 1947.<ref name="AMS-obit">{{cite web |url=https://www.ams.org/news#!class_id=402 |website=[[American Mathematical Society]] |title=Colin J. Bushnell (1947-2021) |date=18 February 2021 |accessdate=8 April 2021}}</ref> He studied mathematics at [[King's College London]], where he received his first class honors undergraduate degree and then a Ph.D. in 1972 under the supervision of [[Albrecht Fröhlich]].<ref name="KCL-memory">{{cite web |url= https://www.kcl.ac.uk/news/in-memory-of-colin-bushnell |website=[[King's College London]] |title= In memory of Colin Bushnell |date=10 February 2021 |accessdate=8 April 2021}}</ref><ref name="genealogy"/>

==Career==
From 1972 to 1975, Bushnell was a lecturer at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]].<ref name="KCL-memory"/> He returned to King's College London in 1975 as Lecturer, before being promoted to Reader in 1985 and Professor in 1990.<ref name="KCL-memory"/> From 1988 to 1989, he was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.ias.edu/scholars/colin-j-bushnell |title=Colin J. Bushnell |website=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |date=9 December 2019 |accessdate=8 April 2021}}</ref> From 1996 to 1997, he was a chairman of the mathematics department and from 1997 to 2004 he was the head of the School of Physical Sciences and Engineering.<ref name="KCL-memory"/> He retired in 2014.<ref name="KCL-memory"/> He died on 1 January 2021 at the age of 73.<ref name="AMS-obit"/>

Bushnell has advised doctoral students including [[Graham Everest]].<ref name="genealogy">{{MathGenealogy|id=60150}}</ref>

==Research==
Bushnell's research included "major contributions to the representation theory of [[reductive group|reductive ''p''-adic groups]] and the study of the [[local Langlands correspondence]]."<ref name="AMS-obit"/>

==Awards==
In 1994, Bushnell was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Zurich (''Smooth representations of p-adic groups: the role of compact open subgroups'').<ref name="KCL-memory"/>

In 1995, Bushnell was awarded the [[Senior Whitehead Prize]].<ref name="KCL-memory"/> In 2002, he became a Fellow of King's College London.<ref name="KCL-memory"/> He was inaugurated in the 2013 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name="KCL-memory"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |website=[[American Mathematical Society]] |accessdate=23 November 2013}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==

*With [[Albrecht Fröhlich]], ''Gauss sums and p-adic division algebras,'' lecture notes in mathematics, vol. 987, Springer Verlag 1983
*With [[Guy Henniart]], ''The local Langlands conjecture for GL(2),'' Springer-Verlag, 2006, {{ISBN|3-540-31486-5}} (Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 335)
*With [[Philip Kutzko]], ''The admissible dual of GL(N) via compact open subgroups,'' [[Annals of Mathematics Studies]] 129, Princeton University Press 1993
